entries.name: {@i Patch}
entries.entry: A crewmember can take the {@action Patch|sw5e-sotg} action as a bonus action.

entries.name: {@i Helm (Fly or Evade)}
entries.entry: A crewmember can take {@action Helm|sw5e-sotg} Fly or Evade as a bonus action.

entries.name: {@i Regenerate Shields}
entries.entry: A crewmember can take the {@action Regenerate Shields|sw5e-sotg} action as a bonus action.

entries.name: {@i Pinpoint Strike}
entries: When your ship occupies the same square occupied by a target ship and the crewmember at the helm makes an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}, as a reaction, they can, before rolling the attack, roll a Pinpoint Strike die, which is a {@dice d4}, and add it to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}.  If the attack requires a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-sotg|saving throw} instead, you may subtract the Pinpoint Strike die from the target's save result.  On a hit or a failed save, the attack deals normal damage that bypasses any shields and directly hits the hull of the target ship. This feature can only be used once per round.
Your ship's Pinpoint Strike die changes when it reaches certain tiers. The die becomes a {@dice d6} at 2nd tier, a {@dice d8} at 3rd tier, a {@dice d10} at 4th tier, and a {@dice d12} at 5th tier.
This feature can be used a number of times equal to your ship's tier. All expended uses are regained when the ship recharges.

entries.name: {@i Retro Thrusters}
entries: When an attacker that a crewmember can see deals damage to your ship with a weapon, they can use their reaction to immediately move the ship up to 50 feet in a direction of their choice, halving the damage your ship takes. The orientation of the ship does not change.
Once this feature has been used, it can't be used again until the ship recharges.
{@optfeature Pinpoint Strike|sw5e-sotg} (Tier 1)
{@optfeature Retro Thrusters|sw5e-sotg} (Tier 2)

entries.name: {@i Blockade Runner}
entries: As a reaction to being hit with an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll} from a Large or larger ship, a deployed pilot can use their reaction to immediately move the ship forward an amount equal to half its {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-sotg|flying speed} (rounded down) and then roll a Blockade Runner die, which is a d4, and subtract it from the triggering {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}, potentially causing it to miss.

Your ship's Blockade Runner die changes when it reaches certain tiers. The die becomes a d6 at 2nd tier, a d8 at 3rd tier, a d10 at 4th tier, and a d12 at 5th tier.This feature can be used a number of times equal to 3 x your ship’s tier. All expended uses are regained when the ship is refitted.

This feature can be used a number of times equal to your ship's tier. All expended uses are regained when the ship is refitted.

entries.name: {@i Blockade Runner}
entries: As a reaction to being hit with an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll} from a Large or larger ship, a crewmember at the helm can use their reaction to immediately move the ship forward an amount equal to half its flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-sotg|speed} (rounded down) and then roll a Blockade Runner die, which is a {@dice d4}, and subtract it from the triggering {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}, potentially causing it to miss.
Your ship's Blockade Runner die changes when it reaches certain tiers. The die becomes a {@dice d6} at 2nd tier, a {@dice d8} at 3rd tier, a {@dice d10} at 4th tier, and a {@dice d12} at 5th tier.
This feature can be used a number of times equal to 3 x your ship's tier. All expended uses are regained when the ship is refitted.
{@optfeature Blockade Runner|sw5e-sotg} (Tier 1)
{@optfeature Concentrated Fire|sw5e-sotg} (Tier 2)

entries.name: {@i Pinpoint Strike}
entries: When your ship occupies the same square occupied by a target ship and the crewmember at the helm makes an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}, as a reaction, they can, before rolling the attack, roll a Pinpoint Strike die, which is a {@dice d4}, and add it to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}.  If the attack requires a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-sotg|saving throw} instead, you may subtract the Pinpoint Strike die from the target's save result.  On a hit or a failed save, the attack deals normal damage that bypasses any shields and directly hits the hull of the target ship. This feature can only be used once per round.
Your ship's Pinpoint Strike die changes when it reaches certain tiers. The die becomes a {@dice d6} at 2nd tier, a {@dice d8} at 3rd tier, a {@dice d10} at 4th tier, and a {@dice d12} at 5th tier.
This feature can be used a number of times equal to your ship's tier. All expended uses are regained when the ship recharges.

entries.name: {@i Retro Thrusters}
entries: When an attacker that a crewmember can see deals damage to your ship with a weapon, they can use their reaction to immediately move the ship up to 50 feet in a direction of their choice, halving the damage your ship takes. The orientation of the ship does not change.
Once this feature has been used, it can't be used again until the ship recharges.
{@optfeature Pinpoint Strike|sw5e-sotg} (Tier 1)
{@optfeature Retro Thrusters|sw5e-sotg} (Tier 2)

entries.name: {@i Damage Control}
entries: Once per turn, as a reaction to being dealt damage by a ship weapon, a crewmember can use their reaction and roll a Damage Control die, which is a {@dice d4}, and subtract it from the damage roll.
Your ship's Damage Control die changes when it reaches certain tiers. The die becomes a {@dice d6} at 2nd tier, a {@dice d8} at 3rd tier, a {@dice d10} at 4th tier, and a {@dice d12} at 5th tier.
This feature can be used a number of times equal to 4 x your ship's tier. All expended uses are regained when the ship undergoes refitting.

entries.name: {@i Versatile Cruiser}
entries: When a crewmember makes an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-sotg|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-sotg|saving throw}, they can use their reaction to have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-sotg|advantage} on the roll. A crewmember can choose to use this feature after they make their roll, but before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails.
This feature can be used a number of times equal to 2 x your ship's tier. All expended uses are regained when the ship undergoes recharging.

entries.name: {@i Pinpoint Strike}
entries: When your ship occupies the same square occupied by a target ship and the crewmember at the helm makes an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}, as a reaction, they can, before rolling the attack, roll a Pinpoint Strike die, which is a {@dice d4}, and add it to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}.  If the attack requires a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-sotg|saving throw} instead, you may subtract the Pinpoint Strike die from the target's save result.  On a hit or a failed save, the attack deals normal damage that bypasses any shields and directly hits the hull of the target ship. This feature can only be used once per round.
Your ship's Pinpoint Strike die changes when it reaches certain tiers. The die becomes a {@dice d6} at 2nd tier, a {@dice d8} at 3rd tier, a {@dice d10} at 4th tier, and a {@dice d12} at 5th tier.
This feature can be used a number of times equal to your ship's tier. All expended uses are regained when the ship recharges.

entries.name: {@i Pinpoint Strike}
entries: When your ship occupies the same square occupied by a target ship and the crewmember at the helm makes an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}, as a reaction, they can, before rolling the attack, roll a Pinpoint Strike die, which is a {@dice d4}, and add it to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}.  If the attack requires a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-sotg|saving throw} instead, you may subtract the Pinpoint Strike die from the target's save result.  On a hit or a failed save, the attack deals normal damage that bypasses any shields and directly hits the hull of the target ship. This feature can only be used once per round.
Your ship's Pinpoint Strike die changes when it reaches certain tiers. The die becomes a {@dice d6} at 2nd tier, a {@dice d8} at 3rd tier, a {@dice d10} at 4th tier, and a {@dice d12} at 5th tier.
This feature can be used a number of times equal to your ship's tier. All expended uses are regained when the ship recharges.

entries.name: {@i Blockade Runner}
entries: As a reaction to being hit with an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll} from a Large or larger ship, a crewmember at the helm can use their reaction to immediately move the ship forward an amount equal to half its flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-sotg|speed} (rounded down) and then roll a Blockade Runner die, which is a {@dice d4}, and subtract it from the triggering {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}, potentially causing it to miss.
Your ship's Blockade Runner die changes when it reaches certain tiers. The die becomes a {@dice d6} at 2nd tier, a {@dice d8} at 3rd tier, a {@dice d10} at 4th tier, and a {@dice d12} at 5th tier.
This feature can be used a number of times equal to 3 x your ship's tier. All expended uses are regained when the ship is refitted.

entries.name: {@i Versatile Frigate}
entries: When a crewmember makes an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-sotg|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-sotg|saving throw} with the ship, they can use their reaction to have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-sotg|advantage} on the roll. A crewmember can choose to use this feature after they make their roll, but before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails.
This feature can be used a number of times equal to 3 x your ship's tier. All expended uses are regained when the ship is refitted.

entries.name: {@i Blockade Runner}
entries: As a reaction to being hit with an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll} from a Large or larger ship, a crewmember at the helm can use their reaction to immediately move the ship forward an amount equal to half its flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-sotg|speed} (rounded down) and then roll a Blockade Runner die, which is a {@dice d4}, and subtract it from the triggering {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}, potentially causing it to miss.
Your ship's Blockade Runner die changes when it reaches certain tiers. The die becomes a {@dice d6} at 2nd tier, a {@dice d8} at 3rd tier, a {@dice d10} at 4th tier, and a {@dice d12} at 5th tier.
This feature can be used a number of times equal to 3 x your ship's tier. All expended uses are regained when the ship is refitted.

entries.name: {@i Versatile Frigate}
entries: When a crewmember makes an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-sotg|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-sotg|saving throw} with the ship, they can use their reaction to have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-sotg|advantage} on the roll. A crewmember can choose to use this feature after they make their roll, but before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails.
This feature can be used a number of times equal to 3 x your ship's tier. All expended uses are regained when the ship is refitted.

entries.name: {@i Pinpoint Strike}
entries: When your ship occupies the same square occupied by a target ship and the crewmember at the helm makes an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}, as a reaction, they can, before rolling the attack, roll a Pinpoint Strike die, which is a {@dice d4}, and add it to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}.  If the attack requires a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-sotg|saving throw} instead, you may subtract the Pinpoint Strike die from the target's save result.  On a hit or a failed save, the attack deals normal damage that bypasses any shields and directly hits the hull of the target ship. This feature can only be used once per round.
Your ship's Pinpoint Strike die changes when it reaches certain tiers. The die becomes a {@dice d6} at 2nd tier, a {@dice d8} at 3rd tier, a {@dice d10} at 4th tier, and a {@dice d12} at 5th tier.
This feature can be used a number of times equal to your ship's tier. All expended uses are regained when the ship recharges.

entries.name: {@i Retro Thrusters}
entries: When an attacker that a crewmember can see deals damage to your ship with a weapon, they can use their reaction to immediately move the ship up to 50 feet in a direction of their choice, halving the damage your ship takes. The orientation of the ship does not change.
Once this feature has been used, it can't be used again until the ship recharges.
{@optfeature Pinpoint Strike|sw5e-sotg} (Tier 1)
{@optfeature Retro Thrusters|sw5e-sotg} (Tier 2)

entries.name: {@i Patch}
entries.entry: A crewmember can take the {@action Patch|sw5e-sotg} action as a bonus action.

entries.name: {@i Pinpoint Strike}
entries: When your ship occupies the same square occupied by a target ship and the crewmember at the helm makes an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}, as a reaction, they can, before rolling the attack, roll a Pinpoint Strike die, which is a {@dice d4}, and add it to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}.  If the attack requires a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-sotg|saving throw} instead, you may subtract the Pinpoint Strike die from the target's save result.  On a hit or a failed save, the attack deals normal damage that bypasses any shields and directly hits the hull of the target ship. This feature can only be used once per round.
Your ship's Pinpoint Strike die changes when it reaches certain tiers. The die becomes a {@dice d6} at 2nd tier, a {@dice d8} at 3rd tier, a {@dice d10} at 4th tier, and a {@dice d12} at 5th tier.
This feature can be used a number of times equal to your ship's tier. All expended uses are regained when the ship recharges.

entries.name: {@i Retro Thrusters}
entries: When an attacker that a crewmember can see deals damage to your ship with a weapon, they can use their reaction to immediately move the ship up to 50 feet in a direction of their choice, halving the damage your ship takes. The orientation of the ship does not change.
Once this feature has been used, it can't be used again until the ship recharges.
{@optfeature Pinpoint Strike|sw5e-sotg} (Tier 1)
{@optfeature Retro Thrusters|sw5e-sotg} (Tier 2)

items.entry: {@action Boost|sw5e-sotg}, {@action Detect|sw5e-sotg}, {@action Direct|sw5e-sotg}, {@action Fire|sw5e-sotg}, {@action Helm|sw5e-sotg}, {@action Interfere|sw5e-sotg}, {@action Patch|sw5e-sotg}, {@action Regenerate Shields|sw5e-sotg}.

items.name: {@i Slam}
items.entry: As an action, a crewmember can activate the SLAM to cause the ship to immediately move forward an amount up to the ship's movement {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-sotg|speed}.

action: {@note On the ship's turn, each crewmember may take one action, limited to their deployment, station, class, ventures, and equipment. Only the helm crewmember can take Helm actions. Direct, Fire, Interfere, and Patch may be taken multiple times on a ship's turn.}

entries.name: {@i Helm (Fly or Evade)}
entries.entry: A crewmember can take {@action Helm|sw5e-sotg} Fly or Evade as a bonus action.

entries.name: {@i Regenerate Shields}
entries.entry: A crewmember can take the {@action Regenerate Shields|sw5e-sotg} action as a bonus action.

entries.name: {@i Pinpoint Strike}
entries: When your ship occupies the same square occupied by a target ship and the crewmember at the helm makes an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}, as a reaction, they can, before rolling the attack, roll a Pinpoint Strike die, which is a {@dice d4}, and add it to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}.  If the attack requires a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-sotg|saving throw} instead, you may subtract the Pinpoint Strike die from the target's save result.  On a hit or a failed save, the attack deals normal damage that bypasses any shields and directly hits the hull of the target ship. This feature can only be used once per round.
Your ship's Pinpoint Strike die changes when it reaches certain tiers. The die becomes a {@dice d6} at 2nd tier, a {@dice d8} at 3rd tier, a {@dice d10} at 4th tier, and a {@dice d12} at 5th tier.
This feature can be used a number of times equal to your ship's tier. All expended uses are regained when the ship recharges.

entries.name: {@i Retro Thrusters}
entries: When an attacker that a crewmember can see deals damage to your ship with a weapon, they can use their reaction to immediately move the ship up to 50 feet in a direction of their choice, halving the damage your ship takes. The orientation of the ship does not change.
Once this feature has been used, it can't be used again until the ship recharges.

entries.name: {@i Versatile Snubfighter}
entries: When a crewmember makes, with the ship, an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-sotg|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-sotg|saving throw}, they can use their reaction to have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-sotg|advantage} on the roll. A crewmember can choose to use this feature after they make their roll, but before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails.
This feature can be used a number of times equal to your ship's tier. All expended uses are regained when the ship is refitted.
{@optfeature Pinpoint Strike|sw5e-sotg} (Tier 1)
{@optfeature Retro Thrusters|sw5e-sotg} (Tier 2)
{@optfeature Auto-Thrusters|sw5e-sotg} (Tier 3)
{@optfeature Versatile Snubfighter|sw5e-sotg} (Tier 3)
{@optfeature Standing By|sw5e-sotg} (Tier 4)

entries.name: {@i Pinpoint Strike}
entries: When your ship occupies the same square occupied by a target ship and the crewmember at the helm makes an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}, as a reaction, they can, before rolling the attack, roll a Pinpoint Strike die, which is a {@dice d4}, and add it to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll}.  If the attack requires a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-sotg|saving throw} instead, you may subtract the Pinpoint Strike die from the target's save result.  On a hit or a failed save, the attack deals normal damage that bypasses any shields and directly hits the hull of the target ship. This feature can only be used once per round.
Your ship's Pinpoint Strike die changes when it reaches certain tiers. The die becomes a {@dice d6} at 2nd tier, a {@dice d8} at 3rd tier, a {@dice d10} at 4th tier, and a {@dice d12} at 5th tier.
This feature can be used a number of times equal to your ship's tier. All expended uses are regained when the ship recharges.
{@optfeature Pinpoint Strike|sw5e-sotg} (Tier 1)

vehicleFluff.name: B-wing/ASF-01 starfighter and B-Wing/E (Tier 3)
entries: The Millennium Falcon is a heavily modified YT-1300f light freighter, and falls under the Medium size category. The ship starts at tier 0. As a tier 0 Medium ship, the Millennium Falcon chooses a role, granting a +1 ASI. We choose "freighter," granting a +1 to the Falcon's Constitution score. As a tier 0 Medium ship, the Millennium Falcon has 5 Hull Dice - which are d8s - and a Constitution modifier of +1. Consequently, the Millennium Falcon has 33 {@variantrule Hull Points|sw5e-sotg|hull points}: 8 + the average for the subsequent four dice (5) + the Constitution modifier for each Hull Die (5 x 1). The Millennium Falcon has shields, so we turn to {@book Chapter 5: Equipment|sw5e-sotg|7|Chapter 5: Equipment} and turn to the "{@book Shields|sw5e-sotg|7|Shields}" section. We select fortress shields to represent the Falcon's very powerful shield systems. As a tier 0 Medium ship, the Falcon has 5 shield Dice - which are d8s - and a Strength modifier of +2. Consequently, the Falcon has 38 Base shield Points: 8 + the average for the subsequent four dice (5) + the Strength modifier for each shield Die (5 x 2). Because fortress shields multiply your Base shield Points by 3/2, the Falcon has a shield Capacity of 57. The Falcon's shield Regeneration rate is 5: the shield die maximum (8) multiplied by the fortress shield shield Regeneration Rate Coefficient (2/3). When the Millennium Falcon progresses to tier 1 it gains the following features: Starship Improvements and Evasive Maneuvers. We record Evasive Maneuvers on the starship sheet. Since the Millennium Falcon is fast, we increase its Strength by 2 with the Ability Score Improvement. This increases the Falcon's Strength Modifier by 1 to +3, adding 5 more to the ship's Base shield Points. It gains an additional Hull Dice, and it’s current and maximum {@variantrule Hull Points|sw5e-sotg|hull points} increases by 6. It also gains an additional shield Die, increasing its Base shield Points by another 8 (5+3). Recalculating the Falcon's shield Capacity gives us 76. Additionally, at tier 0, a Medium ship gets a choice of two {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-sotg|saving throw} proficiencies. For the Falcon, we choose Strength and Dexterity.

When you try to hide your ship, make a Dexterity ({@skill Hide|sw5e-sotg}) check. Until you are discovered or stop hiding, that check is contested by the Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) check of any ship or station that actively searches for signs of your presence. You can't hide from a ship that can perceive you, and if your ship does something to make your ship noticed, you give away your position. In combat, most ships stay alert for danger, so if you come out of hiding and approach a ship, it usually per-ceives you. However, under certain circumstances, the GM might allow you to stay hidden as you approach a ship that is distracted or has some blind spot or de-fect, allowing you to gain {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-sotg|advantage} on an attack before you are perceived. {@b {@i Passive Scan.}} When you hide, there's a chance some-one will notice you even if they aren't searching. To determine whether such a ship notices you, the GM compares your Dexterity ({@skill Hide|sw5e-sotg}) check with that ship's passive Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) score, which equals 10 + the ship's Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) modifier. If the ship has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-sotg|advantage}, add 5. For {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-sotg|disadvantage}, subtract 5. For example, if a 1st-tier ship has a Wisdom of 15 and is proficiently equipped for Scan, it has a passive Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) of 14.

The most important distinction here is the scaling down of the dice. An X-wing's laser cannon deals 1d6 to an enemy X-wing. The perspective for damage here is space. If you need to scale ships to the perspective of players, see {@variantrule Space Versus Ground Scale|sw5e-sotg}. You typically scale damage, {@variantrule Hull Points|sw5e-sotg|hull points}, {@variantrule Shield Points|sw5e-sotg|shield points}, damage reduction, and shield regeneration rate of ships by 10, and vice versa. For Instance, an X-wing's primary weapon may deal 1d6 to ships, but would deal (1d6)x10 to a player, while a player's explosion power would instead deal (8d6)/10 damage (round down) to the X-wing. Because of their size and durability, some GMs may rule that Large and larger ships are simply immune to damage from small arms fire. Additionally, a Tiny starship is Tiny on the space scale, but Huge on the ground scale. Consequently, a Small ship is Gargantuan on the ground scale. Medium and larger ships would be considered colossal. Because starships are not primarily designed to fight individual creatures, Tiny-Large Starships have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-sotg|disadvantage} on attacks versus Large and smaller creatures (and such creatures have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-sotg|advantage} on saves caused by these ships' weapons).

Lastly, while I would love to say that I created everything in this conversion, that wouldn't be entirely true. The following people deserve credit as well: THE /R/SW5E MOD TEAM: Karbacca for the epic {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-sotg|cover} and SW5e logo LordAelfric for the awesome theme Stormchaser6 for his help with the Starships book DarkMesa for writing almost as many archetypes as I have at this point Speedreeder for the epic new website THE REST OF THE JEDI COUNCIL: Grelite for all his help with editing and creation Tomato-andrew for his immense help with the enhanced items Fynikz for his help overhauling and implementing new powers Playking57 for his help with the artwork DrakeRyzer for his work on polishing factions and ships Toddmoonbounce for his help getting the book ready for printing Legobis for creating a whole bunch of monsters THE WEBSITE TEAM: Speedreeder and Tyrzaphir All of the contributors who have been greatly helpful in developing and reviewing new content. You guys are invaluable.

entries: Most Star Wars characters don't work alone, and while some starships can be operated by a single crew member, it is more dynamic—and engaging—to crew a starship with a {@i party}—each member of the party fulfilling a needed role on the ship. Teamwork and cooperation greatly improve your party's chance to survive the unapologetic lethality of spacefaring.

The presence of environmental obstacles also creates a more dynamic battlefield, adding another dimension to the placement and movement of starships. Terrain challenges in space combat necessitate movement and encourage players to be more creative in their actions. The following terrain hazards can be part of any space combat sequence.

vehicleFluff.name: YT-1300 - Iconic (Tier 3)
entries: The Millennium Falcon is a heavily modified YT-1300f light freighter, and falls under the Medium size category. The ship starts at tier 0. As a tier 0 Medium ship, the Millennium Falcon chooses a role, granting a +1 ASI. We choose "freighter," granting a +1 to the Falcon's Constitution score. As a tier 0 Medium ship, the Millennium Falcon has 5 Hull Dice - which are d8s - and a Constitution modifier of +1. Consequently, the Millennium Falcon has 33 {@variantrule Hull Points|sw5e-sotg|hull points}: 8 + the average for the subsequent four dice (5) + the Constitution modifier for each Hull Die (5 x 1). The Millennium Falcon has shields, so we turn to {@book Chapter 5: Equipment|sw5e-sotg|7|Chapter 5: Equipment} and turn to the "{@book Shields|sw5e-sotg|7|Shields}" section. We select fortress shields to represent the Falcon's very powerful shield systems. As a tier 0 Medium ship, the Falcon has 5 shield Dice - which are d8s - and a Strength modifier of +2. Consequently, the Falcon has 38 Base shield Points: 8 + the average for the subsequent four dice (5) + the Strength modifier for each shield Die (5 x 2). Because fortress shields multiply your Base shield Points by 3/2, the Falcon has a shield Capacity of 57. The Falcon's shield Regeneration rate is 5: the shield die maximum (8) multiplied by the fortress shield shield Regeneration Rate Coefficient (2/3). When the Millennium Falcon progresses to tier 1 it gains the following features: Starship Improvements and Evasive Maneuvers. We record Evasive Maneuvers on the starship sheet. Since the Millennium Falcon is fast, we increase its Strength by 2 with the Ability Score Improvement. This increases the Falcon's Strength Modifier by 1 to +3, adding 5 more to the ship's Base shield Points. It gains an additional Hull Dice, and it’s current and maximum {@variantrule Hull Points|sw5e-sotg|hull points} increases by 6. It also gains an additional shield Die, increasing its Base shield Points by another 8 (5+3). Recalculating the Falcon's shield Capacity gives us 76. Additionally, at tier 0, a Medium ship gets a choice of two {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-sotg|saving throw} proficiencies. For the Falcon, we choose Strength and Dexterity.

entries.name: Grade 3 (Universal)
entries: You add an ablative coating to your hull, granting your hull resistance to energy damage.

entries.name: Grade 3 (Universal)
entries: You add an absorbtive capacitor to your shield generator, granting your shields resistance to kinetic damage.

entries.name: Grade 0 (Universal)
entries: While you are in atmosphere, this modification reduces your turn {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-sotg|speed} by 100 feet (min. 50 feet) and grants you a +1 bonus to AC and Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-sotg|saving throws}.

entries.name: Grade 0 (Engineering)
entries: Your ship is equipped with an alternative fuel converter which allows the conversion of materials to a potential fuel source. Over the course of 10 minutes, a crewmember can make a constitution (Regulation) check (DC  = 10 or half the number of days since the ship's last refueling, whichever number is higher). On a success, the ship recovers one unit worth of fuel. This feature can be used a number of times equal to your ship's tier (a minimum of once). All expended uses are regained when the ship undergoes refitting.

entries.name: Grade 0 (Universal)
entries: This modification allows your ship and all of its systems (including weapons) to function underwater.  Your ship gains a swimming {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-sotg|speed} equal to half of its normal {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-sotg|speed}.

entries.name: Grade 0 (Universal)
entries: An anti-boarding system is a robust series of blast doors, cameras, and hidden turrets, reinforcing each portal throughout the ship, as well as directly outside each ship entrance. These features are controllable from the cockpit or in the Security Suite (if it exists) by a crewmember. The anti-boarding system comes with its own power backup in case of main system failure. The reinforced doors can be bypassed with a DC 20 Intelligence ({@item Security kit|sw5e-phb|Security Kit}) check.

entries.name: Grade 0 (Suite)
entries: This suite comes with storage for weapons and armor to outfit a number of crewmembers equal to twice the ship’s suite capacity by size, as shown in the {@b Starship Size Suite Capacity} table. When installed it comes fully stocked with {@item Blaster pistol|sw5e-phb|blaster pistols}, {@item Blaster rifle|sw5e-phb|blaster rifles}, {@item Techblade|sw5e-phb|techblades}, and vibroblades, as well as combat suits, {@item Mesh armor|sw5e-phb|mesh armor}, {@item Battle armor|sw5e-phb|battle armor}, and light and medium shields. The armory is also equipped with both a key and a code lock. The armory can be accessed with a DC 20 Intelligence ({@item Security kit|sw5e-phb|Security Kit}) check. When the armory is accessed, an alarm sounds in the Bridge and Security Suite (if it exists). If a player rolls a 25 or higher on the Intelligence ({@item Security kit|sw5e-phb|Security Kit}) check to unlock the armory, or has the key or code, the alarm can be bypassed. Additionally, it comes with a number of weapon training simulators equal to one-fourth the ship’s suite capacity by size (minimum of one), as shown in the {@b Starship Size Suite Capacity} table. Lastly, when a creature completes a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} involving this suite, they gain {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-sotg|advantage} on the first {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll} they make before the start of their next {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Grade 0 (Operation)
entries: This system adds space for a single Small or Tiny droid crewmember and allows that crewmember to take the {@action Patch|sw5e-sotg} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-sotg} on their turn.  Additionally, this crewmember can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-sotg} to make an Intelligence (Astrogation) check. This modification cannot be installed in a ship that already has Co-Pilot Seat installed.

entries.name: Grade 2 (Engineering)
entries: You upgrade your damage control system. A crewmember can take the {@action Patch|sw5e-sotg} action as a {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-sotg}.  This feature can be used a number of times equal to your ship's tier (a minimum of once). All expended uses are regained when the ship undergoes refitting. Additionally, you can add your ship's intelligence modifier (minimum of +1) to whenever you roll hull dice to regain {@variantrule Hull Points|sw5e-sotg|hull points}. Finally, your ship is expertly equipped for Constitution (Patch) checks.

entries.name: Grade 0 (Weapon)
entries: When you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-sotg|advantage} on the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-sotg|attack roll} and hit, and the lower of the two {@dice d20} rolls would also hit, or when the target ship has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-sotg|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-sotg|saving throw} and fails, and the higher of the two rolls would also fail, you can force the target to make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-sotg|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-sotg|Proficiency Bonus} + the ship's Strength modifier). On a failed save, the ship is {@condition Blinded|sw5e-phb|blinded} until the start of your next turn. If the damaged ship is larger than your ship, it has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-sotg|advantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-sotg|saving throw}. If the damaged ship is smaller than your ship, it instead has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-sotg|disadvantage}.

entries.name: Grade 2 (Engineering)
entries: Your ship has been further modified with a massive grappling harpoon, through which creatures can pass. Your ship is expertly equipped for Strength (Ram) checks. Additionally, when a crewmember takes the Ram action, on a success, the ships become harpooned. While harpooned, your ship and the target ship are {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} as show in the Harpooned and Harpooning Ships {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb} Level tables, below. A crewmember can release the harpooned ship at any time (no action required). The harpooned ship is automatically released if your ship becomes disabled, or if it is forcefully moved more than 100 feet away from your ship.
